results.concept: The Broncos keep saying Bo Nix is on track for camp, but the next quarterback roster move will show whether they actually trust the ankle or are just trying to sound calm.

drafts.option1:
Every Broncos update on Bo Nix is the same. On track, feels good, everything is fine.

Cool. Then the next QB they add tells me what that ankle actually looks like.
drafts.option2:
Saying Bo Nix is on track for camp is free. Carrying only the current QB room is expensive.
If we go shopping for another arm, that is not “depth”. That is “we do not trust the ankle yet.”
drafts.option3:
Broncos fans are gonna treat “Bo is on track” like it is a diagnosis. I am watching the QB transaction like it is the X ray.

Nothing says confidence like signing another passer.

results.concept: The Nuggets say everything is on the table this summer, but nobody knows if that actually includes changing the non-Jokic minutes that keep wrecking games.

drafts.option1:
Nuggets keep saying everything is on the table this summer. Cool. Just make sure the table includes the part of the game where Jokic sits and we immediately forget how to score.

That stretch has been the real GM.
drafts.option2:
If everything is on the table, start with the only thing teams actually target. The non Jokic minutes.

Until we can survive a Jokic rest, the offseason is just arts and crafts.
drafts.option3:
Every summer we talk ourselves into the bench like it is gonna magically behave. Then Jokic sits, the offense turns into hot potato, and the lead evaporates.

Hope is not a rotation.

results.concept: The Avs are switching goalies after one loss even though the other goalie had been rolling.

drafts.option1:
Avs really saw one L and said yeah we are changing goalies. The guy who was rolling gets the classic reward, a seat and a good attitude.

Nothing screams confidence like a quick hook in the crease.
drafts.option2:
I love the logic. Win a few, build a groove, then after one loss we hit the goalie shuffle like the puck is gonna forget who’s in net.

Hot hand meets quick trigger.
drafts.option3:
Fans will call it depth and matchup stuff. Cool. We are basically treating goalie like a TV remote now, one bad scene and we are smashing the button.

Hope the new channel stops odd man rushes.

results.concept: The Rockies keep calling this a development year, but every road series turns into another reminder that the lineup cannot handle left-handed pitching.

drafts.option1:
Every road trip is the same movie. Rockies call it a development year, then a lefty shows up and our lineup starts developing excuses.

Apparently the lesson is swing early, miss often.
drafts.option2:
Rockies saying development year while sending this lineup to face lefties is like giving rookies a pop quiz every night. Same result, same weak contact, same sad box score.

Lefties have it on beginner mode.
drafts.option3:
I respect the optimism. We keep calling it development year like the bats are gonna learn lefties through exposure therapy.

Road series, lefty starter, and suddenly we are right back to bunt thoughts.
